_README: Recall floors for the de-identification detector, keyed on corpus_fingerprint.
These live in data rather than in test source so that changing one is a
reviewable diff in a file whose entire purpose is to be argued about. A test
that hard-codes 0.95 gets edited to 0.90 in a hurry and nobody notices.
THESE ARE REGRESSION GATES, NOT SAFETY CLAIMS. `NAME: 0.10` does not mean a
10% name recall is acceptable. It means 'the regex tier does not detect
names' is now a tested, blame-able fact instead of an assumption, and it is
the baseline the model tier has to beat. The rows that look absurd are the
most valuable lines in this file.
Floors are deliberately well below measured performance. They catch a
catastrophic regression; they do not catch a slide from 0.98 to 0.91. That is
what scorecard.regex.json is for -- CI asserts computed == snapshot, so any
pattern change fails with a diff naming the label that moved.
Computed over the `easy` and `medium` difficulty tiers only. Gating `easy`
alone would be a tautology (the generator and the regex table share an
understanding of the same shapes); gating `hard` would fail the suite for the
wrong reason. The `hard` tier is reported in docs/deid-evaluation.md.
Precision gets a CEILING, not a floor. A precision floor would let a detector
trade recall away; max_over_redaction_rate only stops it trading the other
way, which is what prevents a `.*` patch gaming recall to 1.00.

regex._note: stdlib only; always on; the only tier that runs inline at capture

_note: The default model tier (build spec step 8). Not yet implemented, so
these floors are unenforced until engines/gliner_onnx.py lands --
check_thresholds() reports a missing engine rather than passing
vacuously. Written down now because they are the acceptance criteria
for that step: the model tier's whole justification is beating the
regex tier's NAME 0.368 and LOCATION baseline.

gliner+llm._note: Combined tier. Additive on top of the regex + GLiNER floor.

_note: Reported, gated far lower. Real OCR garble is worse than what the
generator produces (at most two digit-lookalike substitutions per value),
so a number here is a floor on a floor.
